Do you understand English better than you speak it? If so, you're not alone. One of the most common frustrations of even the most advanced English students is that they understand what they read and hear, but struggle to express themselves in spoken exchanges. Why? The answer is simple: language learners have more opportunities to read and listen to the language they’re learning than to speak or write it. However, the only way to improve your speaking skills is through practice, ideally with a native speaker. This is especially true of English, because fluency in English depends to a great degree on its peculiar patterns of stress and intonation.

In these lessons, you will get the practice you need to increase your fluency and reach your other English-related goals. We will get to know one another in a relaxed conversation about ourselves and about topics that interest you. I will provide prompts to help you if you’re not sure what you feel like talking about during the lesson. I will also provide constructive feedback and guidance, based on areas in which you have the most room for improvement. At the end of the lesson, you will have access to a feedback document that contains my notes on any errors you made and ways you can improve. This document can serve as a guide for the practice and study you do on your own, outside of lessons.

Let's practice the most Common questions asked during a school admissions interview (or job interview.)

Topics
1) Body language & facial gestures
2) Storytelling to match target job or school
3) How to minimize weaknesses & increase positives
4) Practice follow-up questions to handle silences or pauses
5) How to research job culture or school mission statements
6) What to do if we don't know an answer
7) Increase confidence & clear communication
8) Understand what questions most likely will be asked

◾  My teaching style is focused on student communication, while offering feedback on how to improve answers.  

◾  We will revise answers & practice the same question several times, until the student feels comfortable and confident.

Method
This is a "Mock interview" class - I pretend to be the interviewer who is asking the Most Common Questions asked during interviews. I will provide the questions during the class and will support students with better answers.

Target Learner
This class is perfect for any learner practicing how to Ace a job interview or a school admissions interview (Beginner - Advanced).  Ages 13-18

Sample Questions
-Tell me about yourself
-Why do you want to attend this school?
-Why are you a good fit for this job?

-Describe your family
-Tell me about your hobbies
-What are your goals at this future job/school?

-What is your biggest strength?
-What is your biggest weakness?

-What are your favorite school subjects?
-How will you contribute to our school / work community?

*We will also learn how to ask follow-up questions when there is a pause or silence in the interview.

teacher_info.about_teacher: As a former high school English teacher, I know that you have to meet students where they are and use materials that interest them in order to reach them. I also know that different students learn differently; that is, some respond better to listening while others are better with seeing information. So I like to tailor lessons to individual students depending on what methods will work best and keep students motivated.
teacher_info.teaching_style: My teaching style is upbeat and energetic, injected with humor. I know that if I'm bored, the student will be too. So I can't be boring. Language learning should be fun anyway, since learning a language also unlocks a new culture. I like to use materials that are already out there in the culture - whether that's children's books, magazines, newspapers, movies or music - to showcase culture along with language. And as a dual U.S./Canadian citizen, I understand the cultures of both countries.
